title: Affine derived direct image reflects isomorphisms for algebraic spaces
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $f:X\to Y$ an affine morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ with their small etale structure sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space]; affine means representable with affine inverse images of affine scheme charts. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and write $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_T)$ for the full subcategory with quasi-coherent cohomology [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Let $Rf_*$ be the total right derived functor of canonical module direct image [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors], computed by K-injective resolutions (a complex $I$ is K-injective when every map from an acyclic complex to $I$ is null-homotopic). Then $Rf_*$ takes $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ into $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ and reflects isomorphisms: for every morphism $u:E\to F$ in $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$, if $Rf_*u$ is an isomorphism, then $u$ is an isomorphism. No boundedness, Noetherian or finite-type assumption is imposed.

source.place: Tag 08II (lemma-affine-morphism); landing in the quasi-coherent subcategory is Tag 08FA (lemma-quasi-coherence-direct-image), applied to an affine morphism.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-space-affine-locality], choose a surjective etale scheme chart $a:V\to Y$ such that $f_V:X_V=X\times_YV\to V$ is an affine scheme morphism. Put $b:X_V\to X$. The base-changed cover $b$ is jointly surjective etale by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. For any $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$, [lem-sfb-space-derived-etale-chart-calculus] gives $b^*K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{X_V})$ and the natural isomorphism $a^*Rf_*K\cong R(f_V)_*b^*K$. No quasi-compactness of $V$ or $X_V$ is asserted or needed.

source.place: Tags 03WG, 03WI; spaces.tex Tag 02X2; spaces-topologies.tex Tag 041F; spaces-perfect.tex Tags 08F2 and 08F4.

proof.text: The affine scheme morphism $f_V$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence]. Under the equivalences of [lem-sfb-scheme-derived-etale-qcoh-comparison], its small-etale derived direct image agrees naturally with its Zariski derived direct image. The latter preserves quasi-coherent cohomology by [lem-pc-derived-direct-image-preserves-qcoh]. Consequently $a^*Rf_*K$ has quasi-coherent cohomology. The cover criterion of [lem-sfb-space-derived-etale-chart-calculus] implies $Rf_*K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$. This proves the landing assertion for every unbounded $K$.

source.place: Tags 071Q and 08GH; perfect.tex lemma-quasi-coherence-direct-image; morphisms.tex Tag 01S7.

proof.text: Now let $u:E\to F$ with $Rf_*u$ invertible. Applying $a^*$ and the natural comparison in Step 1 shows $R(f_V)_*b^*u$ invertible. By [lem-sfb-scheme-derived-etale-qcoh-comparison], transport $b^*u$ through the equivalence from the Zariski quasi-coherent derived category: its Zariski derived image is invertible because the target equivalence reflects isomorphisms. Apply [lem-sc-affine-derived-pushforward-conservative] to $f_V$, which is affine. It makes the transported morphism invertible, and applying the source equivalence gives that $b^*u$ is invertible.

source.place: Tag 08II (lemma-affine-morphism), proof; Tags 071Q and 08GH; perfect.tex Tag 08I8.

proof.text: Exact slice restriction $b^*$ from [lem-sfb-space-derived-etale-chart-calculus] commutes with cohomology: kernels and images are preserved by exactness, so $H^n(b^*u)=b^*H^n(u)$. Since $b^*u$ is invertible, every one of these maps is invertible. A module sheaf map invertible on a covering is invertible: restrict the local inverses to overlaps, where they agree by uniqueness of the inverse, and glue their values on sections by the sheaf axiom. Apply this to the covering $b$ to get that every $H^n(u)$ is invertible. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology] gives that $u$ is invertible. The same argument includes empty covers of the empty space and imposes no boundedness or finiteness hypothesis.
